item.title: Chicago Fed Goolsbee on CNBC (Mace News headlines 21:44-21:52 Taipei Nov 13): 'the Fed has work to do; lately we have not made any progress and inflation is going the wrong way'; 'right now we're not on a path to 2% and we've got to deal with that'; pace and magnitude of rate hikes will be determined by how quickly inflation returns to 2%; overheating demand from AI buildout is compounding supply shock; services inflation incl. medical costs concerning; jobs market looks stable, maybe tightening a little; central bank has work to do to establish credibility. No explicit December size reported in these headlines

item.title: US October PPI (BLS, 08:30 ET / 21:30 Taipei Nov 13): final demand +0.3% m/m (consensus +0.4%; Sep revised up to +1.4% from +1.3%); +6.5% y/y NSA (consensus 6.6%, Sep 6.3%), largest annual rise since Nov 2022. Core (ex food & energy) +0.3% m/m, in line; core y/y 5.0% per FXStreet. Goods +0.5%, services +0.2% (5th straight rise; truck freight +3.9%). Ex food, energy & trade services +0.5% m/m, +4.9% y/y. Reuters: data supports expectations the Fed could keep hiking after December's widely expected hike; CNBC: markets still fully price at least a 25bp December hike
